# A test triggers one copy of a looped node by its index, on every target a
# test can execute on: testdata/indexed_trigger.txtar is the code. The second
# test renders the loop again first -- a longer list, so instances are reused
# at their positions and one is built -- and the indices still name the copies
# in render order.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component main node {
    var items = ["a", "b"]
    var log = ""
    vbox {
        button #swap(text="swap", @click { items = ["c", "d", "e"] })
        for var it = items {
            button #tap(text=it, @click { log = it })
            checkbox #box(label=it, @change(on) { log = "{it} {on}" })
            input #field(value=it, @change(v) { log = "{it}={v}" })
        }
        text(value=log)
    }
}

func testOneCopy(t Test, c main) {
    c.tap[1].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "b")
    c.box[0].change(true)
    t.assert(c.log == "a true")
    c.field[1].change("x")
    t.assert(c.log == "b=x")
}

func testOneCopyAfterTheLoopRendersAgain(t Test, c main) {
    c.swap.click()
    c.tap[2].click()
    t.assert(c.log == "e")
    c.box[1].change(true)
    t.assert(c.log == "d true")
    c.field[0].change(value="y")
    t.assert(c.log == "c=y")
}

window {
    main
}
